decisions.scope: the three legacy distillation fixtures (known-bad / endorsements / acceptable) and every mechanical consumer of them: the known-worse gate and the concordance dashboard. Does NOT apply to v3 warehouse verdicts, which have their own supersession model.
decisions.decision: Where the same (artwork, exact palette) pair carries conflicting v2-3 grades, the LATEST-timestamped grade is its standing verdict and earlier grades are history. Latest grade bad -> hard-gate known-bad entry marked resolvedByRecency; latest grade good -> dropped from known-bad entirely. `contested` now means only conflicting grades sharing an identical timestamp, which recency cannot break; there are none, so all 37 known-bad entries are hard-gate. Membership is the signal: standing-bad palettes were REMOVED from the good-tier files rather than flagged, so the three files are disjoint by standing grade.

fundingCaveats: NO WAREHOUSE RECORDS FUND THIS. The reviewer gave the recency rule conversationally on 2026-08-02, SUPERSEDING an orchestrator decision of warn-never-block made the same day. Both answers are preserved in legacy/README.md because the fixtures were built once under each and the counts differ (35 hard-gate entries then, 37 now).

Recency is a POLICY, not a measurement. It asserts that a later blinded comparison reflects the reviewer’s settled view better than an earlier one. The warehouse epistemology — censored, relative, rendition-scoped — gives no evidence either way; a palette can lose a later pairing for reasons that have nothing to do with the reviewer changing their mind.
The rule turns 3 palettes from good to gated and 3 from gated to good on a corpus of 37 hard-gate entries. It is an ~8% swing in the gate set decided by a tie-break policy.

fundedByArtifacts.what: 137 artworks x 2 variants against the accepted gradient flag. Variant B beats A decisively and consistently: exact ground_type match with the reviewer 16/30 vs 7/30, binary agreement 17/24 vs 8/20, strict kappa vs the flag 0.31 vs 0.21, answers landing on a value that predicts nothing 31% vs 44%. Ordering is the mechanism with a story behind it — under constrained decoding the property order IS the generation order, so B has committed to two cheap facts about the image before answering the hard one.

The probe arm’s human round, and the measurement that parks it. NO MODEL IS INVOLVED: the reviewer answered 180 probes on the same 30 artworks they had already answered directly. The derivation reproduces their own direct tag on only 13/30 (43.3%) — against a reviewer self-consistency noise floor of 0.63. Binary agreement 16/20 with 10 unmappable. The unsure channel built to carry ambiguity was used 1 time in 180 (0.6%) while the reviewer reported the questions as ambiguous.
Cross-model gold-30 and eval-142 scores under identical prompts, schema and decoding. Not hash-pinned here: the gemma3-27b arm was still writing when this record was made.
v2 of the set; group-a.v1 marked frozen and never to be edited; group-a.v3 and group-a.probes.v1 marked superseded.

fundingCaveats: The GOLD-30 IS THE HARD TAIL BY CONSTRUCTION — the 30 artworks are exactly those where the oracle and the accepted flag CONTRADICTED. Every rate computed on them is a rate on hard cases. An arm can win here and lose on the corpus, and vice versa.

ANCHORING CAVEAT, recorded in the analysis itself: the reviewer browsed /oracle-review earlier the same day, which displays their own direct answers for these same 30 artworks. The probe round shows none of them, but the sittings were not separated. The 43.3% is therefore an UPPER BOUND on what two independent sittings would give — which makes the parking decision stronger, not weaker.

The probe arm was parked WITHOUT a model ever running it. What was measured is the derivation against a human, not the instrument against a model. Its Q2/Q3/Q4 questions (are the probes easy, does the inconsistency rate earn its place, does bundling contaminate) are unanswered.

The ground truth in premise-run-1 is an ACCEPTED ALGORITHM DECISION, not an elicited human label, and the reviewer has since ruled (ORACLE_QUESTION_SET.md Appendix R, 2026-08-03) that the published gradient flag is PALETTE-CONDITIONAL — an artwork can support a valid flat palette and a valid gradient palette. Flag agreement is a secondary signal and must never be called accuracy.

Variant B was chosen on a confound the docs name openly: A and B differ in ORDER and in WORDING, so ordering is not cleanly isolated. The criterion arm (variants C, D) was drafted to deconfound it and has not been run.

PREMISE_NEXT.md §14 lists eight sign-off items; the probe set wording, the 729-row derivation table and the human probe round are marked as needing reviewer sign-off. The round was run; the sign-off ledger has not been updated to say so.

decisions.decision: A round's ITEM is one (image, question) answer when the round asks several questions of an image, and one image when it asks one. reviewed and pending are counted on that key, and a batch's declared itemCount must be stated in the same unit, declared as labelUnit. The two conventions had coexisted silently: bcde-validation-1 declares 160 items = 20 artworks x 8 questions, while earlier rounds declared images. A round that declares images-only while asking several questions per image reports progress its own reviewer cannot reconcile, and the mixed convention is exactly what made "how much is left" unanswerable from the warehouse alone.

fundedByArtifacts.what: 160 items over 20 artworks and 8 questions — the round that forced the unit to be named. Its 160 answers sit under 163 warehouse records (3 superseded re-answers).
The finding: itemCount conventions coexist across released batches, and pending counts were computed against the wrong denominator for multi-question rounds.

fundingCaveats: NO WAREHOUSE RECORDS FUND THIS. It is a convention chosen by the warehouse workstream to make two existing conventions distinguishable, not a measurement and not a reviewer ruling.

THE MITIGATION IS DECLARATIVE, SO IT CAN BE DECLARED WRONG. labelUnit is written by the batch designer. A batch that declares images-only while asking several questions per image revives the whole defect, and nothing in the server can catch that from the data.

decisions.scope: The warehouse query layer and every consumer that reads amended records. It does NOT change what may be WRITTEN — the append-time allowlist is unchanged — and it does not retroactively rewrite any stored amendment. It is a read-time refusal, not a migration.
decisions.decision: AMENDABLE_FIELDS is enforced at QUERY time as well as at append time. An amendment patching a field outside the allowlist is dropped when the record is resolved, and the drop is reported rather than silent. Identity, provenance and palette hashes are therefore unrewritable by anything that reaches the file — including a hand edit, a future tool, or an agent with write access — because the reader refuses the patch even if the writer accepted it. Before this, the allowlist lived only in the append path, so the guarantee held exactly as long as every write went through the CLI.

The finding: the append-time allowlist was the whole defence, and the file is a plain JSONL any process can append to.

fundingCaveats: NO WAREHOUSE RECORDS FUND THIS. It is a structural hardening proposed and implemented by the warehouse arm of the adversarial review.

IT DOES NOT PROTECT THE ORIGINAL RECORD. An attacker or a bug that rewrites a base record in place, rather than appending an amendment, is untouched by this — append-only is a convention of the writers, not a property of the filesystem. The defence is git history, and nothing else.
THIRTEEN AMENDMENTS EXIST TODAY AND ALL ARE AGENT-AUTHORED RETRACTIONS OF DERIVED NOTES. There are zero reviewer amendments, so this rule has never yet refused anything in production.

decisions.scope: warehouse recheck --decisions, and how its output is to be read by any agent or reviewer. It does NOT license editing a decision's fundedBy to make a flag go away, and it does not make a flag a defect.
decisions.decision: The funding gate flags four distinct ways evidence can have moved — amended, retracted, superseded, and missing — not just amendment. In particular SUPERSEDED (the reviewer re-answered the item, so the cited record is a draft) is a first-class flag, and RETRACTED counts whenever it happened, including before the decision was made: citing evidence that was already gone is worse than citing evidence that moved afterwards. Consequence, stated so nobody "fixes" it: recheck legitimately reports flagged>0 today. A flag is the instrument telling the truth about a citation list. It is cleared by a NEW decision record with a corrected citation list, never by editing fundedBy in place.

fundedByArtifacts.what: The four flag semantics and the standing expectation, written out with the current expected count.
The recheck implementation.

fundingCaveats: NO WAREHOUSE RECORDS FUND THIS. It is a process rule about the tool that checks warehouse records; it cannot itself be checked by that tool.

THE EXPECTED FLAG COUNT IS A MOVING NUMBER AND MUST NOT BE PINNED IN PROSE. It was 2 before the 2026-08-03 ledger synchronisation and rises whenever a new record cites a list containing a superseded answer. Re-derive it; do not quote a remembered value.

A FLAG STILL HAS TO BE READ. "Expected" does not mean "ignorable" — the check is worthless if flagged>0 becomes background noise nobody opens. The rule is: open every flag, then decide whether the conclusion moved.

decisions.decision: The criterion arm (variants C and D) RAN, and the §4 corpus-wide gate splits. The UNMAPPED criterion passed outright: 0% unmapped under both C and D, against 31-44% under A/B — a large, favourable result. The EXACT-MATCH criterion was not met by any variant (best 16/30 against a required 22/30). C and D also agree with each other on only 46% of artworks, WORSE than A agrees with B (0.4599 against 0.708 raw inter-variant agreement), so two wordings that share B's ordering do not reproduce B: ordering is not sufficient, and the A-to-B difference cannot be attributed to order on the available evidence. Both successors are recorded, deliberately: (a) the gate's OWN pre-registered branch on this outcome is to escalate the §A.5 ground_type vocabulary split as group-a.v3; (b) the CHOSEN direction, per the reviewer's ruling of the same evening, is not (a) but the residual-isolation route — see d-2026-08-03-reviewer-background-via-residual-isolation. Where they disagree, the reviewer's direction governs and the pre-registration is kept visible so nobody later mistakes the change of course for a result.

THE UNMAPPED RESULT IS FAVOURABLE AND UNDER-REPORTED. 0% unmapped is a large improvement that no document carried for a full day. It bears directly on loose end B5 and on design rule 8, and it was measured, not projected.

THE TWO SUCCESSORS ARE NOT EQUIVALENT AND THE RECORD DELIBERATELY KEEPS BOTH. If the residual route fails, the pre-registered escalation is what the campaign already committed to and is the fallback, not a new idea.

decisions.decision: The per-record confidence field is DROPPED from the next schema. The uncertainty signal that does work is inter-variant disagreement, which costs a second decode rather than a field. Keeping a field that a pre-registered criterion twice failed is how a question set accumulates weight without accumulating information.

decisions.scope: Every blinded batch the review server serves, and every claim made about a verdict on the strength of blinding. It does NOT weaken the salt, which stays and does its job; and it does not apply to oracle-validation rounds, which are not blinded comparisons.
decisions.decision: Blinding guarantees exactly one thing: the served payload does not let the batch order be reconstructed from the item hash. The salt closes that channel. It does NOT hide CONTENT-LEVEL ARM IDENTITY, and it structurally cannot — the payload must serve each side's palette in full for the reviewer to judge it. Measured, not argued: a 24-item two-arm batch whose arms differed only in style (one always flat, one always a 2-stop gradient) was unblinded 24/24 = 100% from the served payload alone, by the one-line rule "the side with a non-null gradient is arm-beta". The standing obligation therefore moves to the batch designer: BEFORE treating blinding as a control, ask whether the two arms are separable by any served field (gradient presence, stop count, either collapse flag, the fieldCss geometry token). Phase 2's paradigm bake-off is exactly the shape that fails this test, and it is the round that matters most.
